info.name: Westchester Courier API
info.description:
Westchester Courier NestJS backend - Auth + Delivery modules.

HOW TO USE:
1. Import this collection into Postman.
2. Set the 'baseUrl' collection variable (defaults to http://localhost:8001).
3. Start the API locally: cd westchester-nestjs && npm install && npm run start:dev (fill in .env first - copy from .env.example).
4. Run folders TOP TO BOTTOM in the order they appear - later folders depend on variables captured by earlier ones (JWTs, IDs, OTP codes). Use Postman's collection Runner to execute a whole folder in order, or click through manually. Every Tests-tab script auto-captures whatever the next request needs.
5. Each folder's own requests state their specific prerequisites and needed data in their Description tab.

FOLDER ORDER: Auth Happy Path -> Auth Negative Cases -> Delivery Admin Setup -> Delivery Admin Create & Assign -> Delivery Driver Fulfillment -> Delivery Reject & Cancel -> Delivery Negative Cases.

DEV-MODE CONVENIENCE: in non-production environments, OTP codes are returned directly in API responses (devActivationCode / devVerificationCode) instead of only being emailed, so this collection is testable without a real inbox. Must never be enabled in production.

request.description: PREREQUISITE: '3. Create Delivery'. No @Roles restriction on this route - both ADMIN and DRIVER tokens work, but a DRIVER only succeeds if the delivery is assigned to them (a service-level ownership check, not a route guard). Used here with the admin token.
PREREQUISITE: '3. Create Delivery' AND Auth step 3 (driverUserId). Stays PENDING after assignment - the driver still has to accept it.
Query params are all optional. Remove '?status=PENDING' to see every delivery.
PREREQUISITE: '3. Create Delivery'. Only works while status is PENDING.

PREREQUISITE: Auth folder step 3 (driver token). Powers the Figma 'Home' screen — pendingCount, activeCount, completedToday, and completedLast7Days (a day-by-day count used for the chart). NOTE: the exact chart metric in Figma couldn't be confirmed field-by-field — this returns 'deliveries completed per day' as the best available proxy without exact design data. Flag this if the real design tracks something else (e.g. earnings).

exec: pm.test('Message indicates created or updated', function () { const m = pm.response.json().message; pm.expect(m).to.match(/Created|Updated/); });

request.description: Confirms the PATCH above actually persisted.
